logic_errors.contract_basis: The documented diagnostic exception rule protects the primary failure (journal guide:65). It does not specify suppression of sole process-exit/cancellation origins. The unchanged shared close_owned propagates a nonlocal close failure in the absence of a primary (rathena_runtime_io:28-36). The review failure model requires origin preservation, not silent consumption of a new KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit/GeneratorExit/custom cancellation arising on the supported public close path. Conservative unresolved status is appropriate but is not propagation.
logic_errors.actual_evidence: Four fresh sole-diagnostic cases fail after actual normal close, with only owned-fd os.fstat patched. Each has a preceding real append/True acknowledgement, a single reached diagnostic, unpatched EBADF, separate-process lock acquisition, borrowed root valid, and unresolved/diagnostic_failed. The exact injected origin retains its fault_diagnostic traceback but the caller sees None. An additional four reached cases with a real-close wrapper independently reproduce this behavior. Four contrasted active-primary OSError + diagnostic nonlocal cases pass and preserve the exact primary; that secondary suppression remains intentional.
logic_errors.calibration: Not a false physical-release finding: the descriptor was actually released and an independent process could flock. It is loss of sole control flow. Eight failing parameterized executions are two distinct oracle variants, not eight defects. Parent-owned pure-diagnostic oracle was read, not run or edited; this report relies on newly owned fresh executions.
